Let
\[
A(s)=\iint_T \Delta^2 (xyz)^{-s}\,dx\,dy.
\]
For \(0<c<1\), Mellin inversion gives
\[
I_n=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{c-i\infty}^{c+i\infty}\Gamma(s)n^{-s}A(s)\,ds.
\]

Use
\[
\Delta^2=(x-y)^2(y-z)^2(z-x)^2
=q^2-4q^3-4r+18qr-27r^2,
\]
where
\[
q=xy+yz+zx,\qquad r=xyz.
\]
Writing
\[
D_{ijk}(s)=\iint_T x^{i-s}y^{j-s}z^{k-s}\,dx\,dy
=\frac{\Gamma(i+1-s)\Gamma(j+1-s)\Gamma(k+1-s)}
{\Gamma(i+j+k+3-3s)},
\]
expansion of the symmetric polynomial gives
\[
A(s)=3D_{220}-2D_{111}-12D_{330}-72D_{321}+54D_{221}-51D_{222}.
\]

The pole at \(s=1\) is
\[
A(s)=-\frac1{10(s-1)}+O(1),
\]
so its Mellin residue contributes
\[
\frac1{10n}.
\]

Now put \(u=s-2\). Around \(s=2\), using
\[
\Gamma(-u)=-\frac1u-\gamma+O(u),\qquad
\Gamma(-1-u)=\frac1u+\gamma-1+O(u),
\]
one obtains
\[
A(2+u)=-\frac6{u^2}-\frac{21}{u}+O(1).
\]
Also
\[
\Gamma(2+u)=1+(1-\gamma)u+O(u^2),
\]
hence
\[
\Gamma(2+u)A(2+u)
=-\frac6{u^2}+\frac{6\gamma-27}{u}+O(1).
\]
Since
\[
n^{-2-u}=n^{-2}(1-u\log n+O(u^2)),
\]
the pole at \(s=2\) contributes
\[
-\operatorname*{Res}_{s=2}\left(\Gamma(s)n^{-s}A(s)\right)
=
\frac{-6\log n+27-6\gamma}{n^2}.
\]

Therefore
\[
I_n=\frac1{10n}+\frac{-6\log n+27-6\gamma}{n^2}+o(n^{-2}).
\]
Thus
\[
n^2I_n-\frac n{10}+6\log n\to 27-6\gamma.
\]

\[
\boxed{27-6\gamma}
\]
